title: Starmer plays down prospect of retaliatory tariffs against US over Greenland
summary: PM says US tariffs are in no one’s interests – and Greenland row should be resolved through ‘calm discussion’ Keir Starmer has played down the prospect of retaliatory tariffs on the US, after Donald Trump threatened to impose fresh levies against Nato allies if a deal over Greenland is not reached. The prime minister said US tariffs would damage the British economy and were “in no one’s interests”, despite growing pressure domestically to take a more forceful response. The UK would prefer a “calm discussion” with allies, he added. Continue reading...

title: Canadians still worried about economy, remain cautious about spending
